### Europe’s Record Wildfires

Firefighters in France and Spain are battling some of the largest wildfires in their history, with Spain declaring its first national wildfire emergency. French President Emmanuel Macron is chairing a crisis meeting to determine a response. The fires in France have created pyrocumulonimbus clouds, which generate their own thunderstorms and lightning. Laurent Nuñez, the French interior minister, estimated that over 13,500 fire outbreaks have been recorded since the start of the fire season, marking an unprecedented number. France has deployed approximately 2,500 firefighters and 1,500 military personnel, alongside 18 aircraft, as both countries brace for another heat wave.

Roughly 330,000 people in both countries have been ordered to evacuate, one of the continent’s largest evacuation efforts since World War II. In France, a complex of fires in the Gironde department has merged into a massive blaze just outside Bordeaux, burning roughly 104,000 acres, destroying at least 240 homes, and forcing 220,000 people to flee, some via rescue boats. In Spain, wildfires near Madrid and in the province of Ávila have burned over 190,000 acres, forcing more than 60,000 from their homes and prompting a national wildfire emergency declaration.

French President Macron remarked that the current situation is the most challenging recorded, surpassing any previous crises since World War II. The spread of the fires has slowed, and some evacuees have been permitted to return home, yet containment remains elusive, with the potential for further spread.

### Quick Hits: Today’s Top Stories

#### Saudi Arabia Comes Under Drone Attack
Saudi Arabia’s Defense Ministry reported that armed forces shot down several drones targeting oil facilities in the eastern region, attributed to Iraq-based, Iran-aligned militias. Jordan and Iraq also reported drone attacks, while the Israel Defense Forces intercepted two drones near the Jordanian border. The ongoing conflict with Iran has led Saudi Arabia to reroute crude oil shipments via the East-West Pipeline to Red Sea export terminals, within the range of Yemen's Houthi group, who have claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure.

#### Israel Expands West Bank Deployment
The Israel Defense Forces have deployed two additional battalions to the West Bank, raising the total to 26 amid escalating tensions between settlers and Palestinians following a deadly shooting incident. The incident resulted in the deaths of four Palestinians and two Israelis. Israeli police arrested nine suspects during raids, including the father of the shooter. Over 1,200 attacks by settlers have been recorded in the West Bank since the beginning of the year.

#### Sen. Rand Paul Releases Fauci’s Diaries
Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky has released over 1,100 pages of Dr. Anthony Fauci’s diaries, documenting his experiences during the COVID-19 pandemic. The release coincides with Fauci's upcoming testimony before the Senate regarding the origins of the pandemic. The entries reportedly reveal Fauci's private estimates of the death rate being significantly lower than public statements, and his growing disenchantment with former President Trump.

### Europe Continues to Battle Record Fires
With wildfires reaching unprecedented levels, firefighters in France and Spain face a challenging season. Spain has declared its first national wildfire emergency as conditions worsen. Macron's government has mobilized military resources to assist in firefighting efforts, while the EU has dispatched aerial support. Experts warn that climate conditions, including rising temperatures and persistent dryness, are exacerbating the fire risk across Europe.
